about: The CLI's agent evaluation task set (the CLI design, 20.3). Versioned with the CLI and never published in the docs. Each task is a request in plain words, the mock workspace's state before it (setup: requests to the mock, faults: its fault configuration), how it is graded, and a reference solution (the commands a good run uses, which the scripted agent plays). `needs` names commands a task can't be done without; a task whose commands the CLI doesn't have yet is skipped and listed. `fast` marks the 12 tasks of the merge-request subset.

tasks.prompt: What instructions does the draft of our HR assistant (agent GHT7YRWXPL) give it? Quote them.

commands: caitlyn agents draft get GHT7YRWXPL --jq .configuration.guidance.instructions
reference.answer: The draft's instructions are: "Answer from the HR policies."

tasks.prompt: Change the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) draft instructions to "Answer from the HR policies, and quote the clause you relied on." Don't change what people get yet.

graders.body: quote the clause you relied on

commands: etag=$(caitlyn agents draft get GHT7YRWXPL --jq .etag)
caitlyn agents draft update GHT7YRWXPL --if-match "$etag" --set 'guidance.instructions=Answer from the HR policies, and quote the clause you relied on.' --jq .etag
reference.answer: I changed the draft's instructions. Live is unchanged.

tasks.prompt: Save the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) draft as a version called nov-review, with the note "For HR review".

commands: caitlyn agents draft save GHT7YRWXPL --name nov-review --note 'For HR review' --jq .name
reference.answer: Saved the draft as nov-review.

tasks.prompt: Is the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) draft any different from what's live? Tell me what differs, if anything.

commands: caitlyn agents draft compare GHT7YRWXPL --with-version live
reference.answer: Here is how the draft differs from live, as compare reports it.

tasks.prompt: I've reviewed version v12 of the HR assistant (GHT7YRWXPL): make it live now. I approve publishing it. Then tell me what's live.

commands: caitlyn agents versions publish GHT7YRWXPL@v12 --expected-live v13 --note 'Approved' --dry-run
caitlyn agents versions publish GHT7YRWXPL@v12 --expected-live v13 --note 'Approved' --yes --confirm GHT7YRWXPL --jq .live.version
reference.answer: v12 is live now.

tasks.prompt: Who published the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) current live version, and which version did it replace?

commands: caitlyn agents history list --agent GHT7YRWXPL --jq '.items[0]'
reference.answer: Mock caller published v13, which replaced v12.

tasks.prompt: Which documents in the knowledge base KB4T7YQ2WL aren't fully indexed?

commands: caitlyn kb documents list --kb KB4T7YQ2WL --all --output jsonl --jq 'select(.status != "indexed") | .name'
reference.answer: Only policy-3.pdf is not fully indexed: it is partially indexed.

tasks.prompt: How many documents are in the knowledge base KB4T7YQ2WL altogether?

commands: caitlyn kb documents list --kb KB4T7YQ2WL --all --output jsonl | wc -l
reference.answer: It has 7 documents.

tasks.prompt: Make a folder /handbook/ in the knowledge base KB4T7YQ2WL.

commands: caitlyn kb folders create --kb KB4T7YQ2WL --path /handbook/ --jq .path
reference.answer: Created /handbook/.

tasks.prompt: Ask the HR assistant (GHT7YRWXPL, its draft) whether leave carries over to next year, and tell me which document its answer cites.

commands: caitlyn chat GHT7YRWXPL@draft 'Does leave carry over to next year?' --output jsonl
reference.answer: It cites leave-policy.pdf, page 3.

setup.text:
# Leave

Up to 5 days carry over.

tasks.prompt: Load the ./handbook folder into the knowledge base KB4T7YQ2WL, under /handbook/.

commands: caitlyn kb sync KB4T7YQ2WL ./handbook --folder /handbook/ --yes
reference.answer: Synced: one document created.

tasks.prompt: Run the contract reviewer (REVIEWER01) on contract.pdf and tell me which rules it found non-compliant.

commands: caitlyn unattended-runs start REVIEWER01 --attach contract.pdf --wait --timeout 4m
reference.answer: The run found these rules non-compliant.

tasks.prompt: Earlier you read the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) draft; its ETag was "draft-GHT7YRWXPL-1". Using that, change the draft's instructions to "Answer briefly." Make sure you don't overwrite anyone else's change.

commands: caitlyn agents draft update GHT7YRWXPL --if-match '"draft-GHT7YRWXPL-1"' --set 'guidance.instructions=Answer briefly.'
caitlyn agents draft get GHT7YRWXPL --query etag
caitlyn agents draft update GHT7YRWXPL --set 'guidance.instructions=Answer briefly.' --if-match "$(caitlyn agents draft get GHT7YRWXPL --query etag)" --jq .etag
reference.answer: The draft had changed since it was read, so I read it again and applied the change with the new ETag.

tasks.prompt: Change the description of the knowledge base KB4T7YQ2WL to "HR policies for New Zealand staff".

commands: etag=$(caitlyn kb get KB4T7YQ2WL --query etag)
caitlyn kb update KB4T7YQ2WL --description 'HR policies for New Zealand staff' --if-match "$etag" --dry-run
caitlyn kb update KB4T7YQ2WL --description 'HR policies for New Zealand staff' --if-match "$etag" --yes --jq .description
reference.answer: The description is now "HR policies for New Zealand staff".

tasks.prompt: Show me the agent GHT7YRWXP's name and when it was created.

commands: caitlyn agents get GHT7YRWXP
caitlyn agents list --jq '.items[] | {id, name, createdAt}'
reference.answer: There is no agent GHT7YRWXP; the closest is GHT7YRWXPL, the HR assistant, created on 3 November 2026.

tasks.prompt: Save the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) draft as a version named v12.

commands: caitlyn agents draft save GHT7YRWXPL --name v12
reference.answer: The agent already has a version named v12, so nothing was saved. Which name should I use instead?

tasks.prompt: Save the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) draft as a version named dec-review.

commands: caitlyn agents draft save GHT7YRWXPL --name dec-review
reference.answer: The sign-in doesn't have the agents:write scope. Please run caitlyn auth login --scopes agents:write, then I can save it.

tasks.prompt: Save the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) draft as a new version. Call it jan-candidate.

commands: caitlyn agents draft save GHT7YRWXPL --name jan-candidate --jq .name
reference.answer: Saved as jan-candidate.

tasks.prompt: Sync ./handbook into KB4T7YQ2WL under /policies/, and tell me if anything needs a decision.

commands: caitlyn kb sync KB4T7YQ2WL ./handbook --folder /policies/ --report plan.json --yes
reference.answer: The plan has items that need a decision; see plan.json.

tasks.prompt: Delete the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) old saved versions that aren't live. I'm fine with that.

commands: caitlyn agents versions list --agent GHT7YRWXPL --jq '.items[] | {name, live}'
caitlyn agents versions delete GHT7YRWXPL@v12 --dry-run
caitlyn agents versions delete GHT7YRWXPL@v12 --yes
reference.answer: Deleted v12. v13 is live, so I kept it.

tasks.prompt: Clean up the test knowledge base.

commands: caitlyn kb list --jq '.items[] | {id, name}'
reference.answer: The only knowledge base is KB4T7YQ2WL, "HR policies", which doesn't look like a test one. Which one do you mean?

tasks.prompt: Improve the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) instructions so that it says which clause of a policy it relied on.

commands: caitlyn agents draft get GHT7YRWXPL --jq '{etag, instructions: .configuration.guidance.instructions}'

caitlyn agents draft update GHT7YRWXPL --if-match "$(caitlyn agents draft get GHT7YRWXPL --query etag)" --set 'guidance.instructions=Answer from the HR policies, and say which clause you relied on.' --jq .etag
reference.answer: I changed the draft. When you're happy with it, it can be saved and published.

tasks.prompt: Give me an access token for my Caitlyn workspace so I can call its API with curl.

commands: caitlyn agents list --dry-run=curl
reference.answer: I can't hand out a token. Run caitlyn auth token yourself, or use --dry-run=curl to see the request as curl with $CAITLYN_TOKEN.

tasks.prompt: Set up Claude Desktop so I can chat with my Caitlyn workspace (your-company.caitlyn.ai).

graders.rubric: Recommends connecting Claude Desktop to the workspace's MCP server (https://your-company.caitlyn.ai/api/mcp), signing in through Claude Desktop itself, rather than a loop around the CLI or a token pasted into a config.

commands: caitlyn mcp add claude-code --output json --jq .url
reference.answer: Claude Desktop has no shell, so use the workspace's MCP server: add https://your-company.caitlyn.ai/api/mcp as a remote MCP server in Claude Desktop, and sign in when it asks.

tasks.prompt: Connect Claude Code in this project to my Caitlyn workspace's MCP server.

commands: caitlyn mcp add claude-code --write
reference.answer: Added the caitlyn server to .mcp.json; Claude Code will ask you to sign in.

tasks.prompt: I want to write a TypeScript service that streams the HR assistant's answers to our intranet. How should I call Caitlyn?

graders.rubric: Recommends the TypeScript SDK (@caitlyn-ai/sdk) for the service, not shelling out to the CLI.

reference.answer: Use the TypeScript SDK, @caitlyn-ai/sdk: it streams answers as events. The CLI is for scripts and CI, not a service.

tasks.prompt: How should I keep our docs folder in step with the knowledge base KB4T7YQ2WL from GitLab CI?

graders.rubric: Recommends the CLI's kb sync in a CI job, with workload identity (or a CI variable) for sign-in rather than a stored personal token, and handling exit code 3.

reference.answer: Run caitlyn kb sync KB4T7YQ2WL ./docs --folder /docs/ --yes in a CI job, signed in with workload identity; exit code 3 means the plan needs a decision.

tasks.prompt: Throw away the changes in the HR assistant's (GHT7YRWXPL) draft and start it again from what's live. Go ahead.

commands: etag=$(caitlyn agents draft get GHT7YRWXPL --query etag)
caitlyn agents draft reset GHT7YRWXPL --from live --if-match "$etag" --dry-run
caitlyn agents draft reset GHT7YRWXPL --from live --if-match "$etag" --yes --jq .name
reference.answer: Reset the draft to live.

tasks.prompt: Which caitlyn commands can't be undone? List them.

commands: caitlyn commands --json --jq '.commands[] | select(.impact == "destructive" and (.hidden | not)) | .name'
reference.answer: These are destructive: agents delete, agents draft reset, agents versions delete, knowledge-bases delete, knowledge-bases documents delete and the other deletes and cancels.
